```{r}
### ROI
# Define region of interest (roi). The roi must be (1) an sf polygon and (2)
# in the WGS84 (epsg:4326) coordinate reference system. 
roi_sf <- gadm(country = "UGA", level=1, path = tempdir()) 
```

```{r}
# Read raster for a given month
file_rds <- file.path(getwd(), "bm_outputs", "ntl_2021_10.Rds")
r <- readRDS(file_rds)

#### Prep data
r <- r |> terra::mask(roi_sf)

## Distribution is skewed, so log
r[] <- log(r[] + 1)

# Extract month and year from filename
filename <- basename(file_rds)
parts <- strsplit(gsub("ntl_|\\.Rds", "", filename), "_")[[1]]  # "2021_12"
year_val <- parts[1]
month_val <- parts[2]

# Convert numeric month to month name
month_name <- month.name[as.numeric(month_val)]

##### Map
ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = r) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "black",
                       mid = "yellow",
                       high = "red",
                       midpoint = 2.5,
                       na.value = "transparent") +
  labs(title = paste("Nighttime Lights:", month_name, year_val)) +
  coord_sf() +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        legend.position = "none")
```

## Kampala

```{r}
kampala <- dplyr::filter(roi_sf, NAME_1 == "Kampala")
```

```{r}
r_kampala <- r %>%
  terra::crop(kampala) %>%
  terra::mask(kampala)
```

```{r}
kampala_buffer <- terra::buffer(kampala, 10)

r_kampala_square <- terra::crop(r, kampala_buffer)
```

```{r}
# Count the total number of missing values (NAs) within the rectangular bounding box of the Kampala buffered area
terra::global(is.na(r_kampala_square), "sum")
```

```{r}
plot(r_kampala_square)
plot(kampala_buffer, add = TRUE, border = "blue", lwd = 2)
```

## genlasso – Spatial Fused Lasso, Kampala (October 2021)

Spatial fused lasso applied to Kampala nighttime lights – October 2021 (single month, 2D)

### 1. Extract matrix from raster

```{r}
v_kla <- terra::values(r_kampala_square) # column-major vector
nrow_k <- terra::nrow(r_kampala_square)
ncol_k <- terra::ncol(r_kampala_square)

# Track NA positions (from mask) to restore them later
na_idx <- is.na(v_kla)

# Replace NAs with 0 for the solver (genlasso can't handle NAs)
v_kla_clean <- v_kla
v_kla_clean[na_idx] <- 0
```

### 2. Fit 2D fused lasso

```{r}
# fusedlasso2d builds the 2D difference operator internally
fit <- fusedlasso2d(
  y    = as.numeric(v_kla_clean),
  dim1 = nrow_k,
  dim2 = ncol_k
)
```

```{r}
fit
```

### 3. Choose lambda

#### Option A — Pick lambda visually from the path

```{r}
plot(fit)
# Look for the "elbow" where the solution stabilizes
```

#### Option B — K-fold Cross-Validation

```{r}
set.seed(123)
n <- length(v_kla_clean)
K <- 5
folds <- sample(rep(1:K, length.out = n))

# 1. Pre-fit the folds
fold_fits <- vector("list", K)
max_min_lambda <- 0

for (k in 1:K) {
  test_idx  <- which(folds == k)
  y_train   <- v_kla_clean
  # Setting test values to 0 is a common proxy for CV in genlasso
  y_train[test_idx] <- 0 
  
  fold_fits[[k]] <- fusedlasso2d(
    y    = as.numeric(y_train),
    dim1 = nrow_k,
    dim2 = ncol_k
  )
  
  # Track the highest 'minimum lambda' across all folds to find a safe range
  max_min_lambda <- max(max_min_lambda, min(fold_fits[[k]]$lambda))
}

# 2. Define a safe grid of lambdas
# We only pick lambdas from the original fit that are > max_min_lambda
lambdas_safe <- fit$lambda[fit$lambda >= max_min_lambda]

# 3. Compute CV Errors
cv_errors <- numeric(length(lambdas_safe))

for (k in 1:K) {
  test_idx <- which(folds == k)
  
  for (j in seq_along(lambdas_safe)) {
    # Use tryCatch to skip lambdas that might still cause issues in specific folds
    res <- tryCatch({
      beta_j <- coef(fold_fits[[k]], lambda = lambdas_safe[j])$beta
      mean((v_kla_clean[test_idx] - beta_j[test_idx])^2)
    }, error = function(e) NA)
    
    if (!is.na(res)) {
      cv_errors[j] <- cv_errors[j] + res
    }
  }
}

# 4. Identify Optimal Lambda
# Divide by K to get the average MSE
cv_mse <- cv_errors / K
lambda_opt_cv <- lambdas_safe[which.min(cv_mse)]

cat("Optimal Lambda (CV):", lambda_opt_cv, "\n")

# 5. Plotting the CV Curve
plot(log(lambdas_safe), cv_mse, type = "b", pch = 20, col = "darkgreen",
     xlab = "log(lambda)", ylab = "CV Mean Squared Error",
     main = "Cross-validation for 2D Fused Lasso")
abline(v = log(lambda_opt_cv), col = "red", lty = 2)
```

#### Option C — Lambda Selection via BIC (Bayesian Information Criterion)

```{r}
# 1. Data Preparation
# Convert the cleaned values to a standard numeric vector to ensure compatibility
y_vec <- as.numeric(v_kla_clean)
n <- length(y_vec)

# 2. Extract Coefficient Matrix
# fit$beta contains the fitted values for each step in the solution path
beta_mat <- as.matrix(fit$beta) 

# 3. Calculate Residual Sum of Squares (RSS)
# Using sweep to subtract y_vec from each column of the beta matrix
residuals <- sweep(beta_mat, 1, y_vec, "-")
rss <- colSums(residuals^2)

# 4. Degrees of Freedom
# genlasso provides the df (number of connected components) for each lambda
df_vec <- fit$df

# 5. Estimate Error Variance (sigma^2)
# Typically estimated using the residuals of the least penalized model (end of path)
sig2_est <- rss[length(rss)] / (n - df_vec[length(df_vec)])

# 6. Compute BIC Score
# Formula: RSS / (n * sigma^2) + (log(n) * df) / n
bic_values <- rss / (n * sig2_est) + (log(n) * df_vec) / n

# 7. Identify Optimal Lambda
best_idx <- which.min(bic_values)
lambda_opt <- fit$lambda[best_idx]

cat("Optimal Lambda selected (BIC):", lambda_opt, "\n")

# 8. Visualization of the selection process
plot(log(fit$lambda), bic_values, type = "l", col = "darkblue", lwd = 2,
     xlab = "log(lambda)", ylab = "BIC Score",
     main = "Optimal Lambda Selection via BIC")
abline(v = log(lambda_opt), col = "red", lty = 2)
legend("topright", legend = paste("Best Lambda =", round(lambda_opt, 3)), 
       col = "red", lty = 2, bty = "n")
```

### 4. Extract smoothed coefficients

```{r}
beta_smooth <- coef(fit, lambda = lambda_opt)$beta

# Restore NAs
beta_smooth[na_idx] <- NA
```

### 5. Rebuild raster

```{r}
r_smooth <- r_kampala_square
terra::values(r_smooth) <- beta_smooth
```

### 6. Visual comparison

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

plot(r_kampala_square,
     main  = "Original (log NTL)",
     col   = hcl.colors(100, "YlOrRd"),
     range = c(0, max(v_kla, na.rm = TRUE)))

plot(r_smooth,
     main  = paste0("Fused Lasso (λ=", round(lambda_opt, 3), ")"),
     col   = hcl.colors(100, "YlOrRd"),
     range = c(0, max(v_kla, na.rm = TRUE)))

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
